title: Activated Alumina Adsorber

introduction.definition: An activated alumina adsorber passes a gas or liquid down through a fixed bed of porous aluminium-oxide beads supported on graded ceramic balls. The beads adsorb water or contaminants such as fluoride, arsenic or acids. The working (mass-transfer) zone moves down the bed until breakthrough, when the bed is regenerated or replaced.
applications: Drying of air, gases and liquids
Fluoride and arsenic removal from drinking water
HCl and acid removal in refinery streams
key_points: Graded ceramic balls support the bed
introduction.summary: An activated alumina adsorber passes a gas or liquid down through a fixed bed of porous aluminium-oxide beads. The beads adsorb water (drying) or contaminants such as fluoride, arsenic or acids. The working zone moves down the bed until breakthrough, then the bed is regenerated or replaced.

pressure.description: The bed works from the inlet down: the top becomes saturated (red), the mass-transfer zone (orange) moves down, and the outlet stays clean until the zone reaches the bottom — breakthrough. Activated alumina is used for drying gases and liquids (to dew points around −40 °C), fluoride and arsenic removal from water, and HCl/acid removal; it is regenerated by heating (drying duty) or chemically (e.g. caustic and acid for fluoride).

video_tutorials.title: Activated Alumina Adsorber — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Activated Alumina Adsorber.
An activated alumina adsorber passes a gas or liquid down through a fixed bed of porous aluminium-oxide beads supported on graded ceramic balls.
The beads adsorb water or contaminants such as fluoride, arsenic or acids.
The working (mass-transfer) zone moves down the bed until breakthrough, when the bed is regenerated or replaced.

Typical applications include drying of air, gases and liquids; fluoride and arsenic removal from drinking water; HCl and acid removal in refinery streams; transformer-oil and liquid hydrocarbon drying.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Activated Alumina Adsorber — Operation

script.narration: How the Activated Alumina Adsorber works.
Fluid enters through the inlet distributor.
It passes down through the alumina bed.
Contaminants are adsorbed in the mass-transfer zone.
The saturated zone grows from the top.
Treated fluid leaves through the bottom collector.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
The bed works from the inlet down: the top becomes saturated (red), the mass-transfer zone (orange) moves down, and the outlet stays clean until the zone reaches the bottom — breakthrough.

video_tutorials.title: Activated Alumina Adsorber — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Activated Alumina Adsorber.
Monitor outlet quality and ΔP.
Regenerate at breakthrough.
Replace alumina; inspect internals.
Watch for channelling: early breakthrough. Common cause: poor distribution, bed settling.
Watch for bead breakdown: fines, ΔP rise. Common cause: liquid water slugs, thermal shock.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
